capability.video.gen.description: Allows the app to generate video via a unit (host-mediated call and persistence, consumes account quota; runs minutes for long tasks; artifacts served from the app's own URL).

capability.voice.read.description: Allows the app to enumerate host voice accounts (separate stt/tts lists; metadata like name/provider/model, never API keys).

capability.voice.stt.description: Allows the app to call speech recognition services, transcribing audio into text (consumes account quota).
capability.voice.stt.title: Speech-to-text (STT)
capability.voice.tts.description: Allows the app to call speech synthesis services, converting text into audio (consumes account quota).
capability.voice.tts.title: Text-to-speech (TTS)

onboarding.guide.appPanel.body: This switch toggles between two sidebar panels: “Build”, your projects and agent workbench, and “Apps”, the launcher for installed Spore Apps. Click it to switch into the Apps panel.
onboarding.guide.appPanel.title: Build & Apps panels
onboarding.guide.createAgent.body: Now that you have a project, create an agent to work in it. Click “New Agent” and pick a coder agent — it will handle coding tasks within this project.
onboarding.guide.createAgent.title: Create an agent
onboarding.guide.createProject.body: You don't have a project yet. Click “New Project” to create one — a project is where your agents live and work. You can open an existing folder or start from scratch.
onboarding.guide.createProject.title: Create your first project
onboarding.guide.finish.body: That is the core sporemind loop: intent → break down → execute → review → summarize. Want to walk through the guide again? Open Settings → About and click Replay guide.
onboarding.guide.finish.title: You're all set
onboarding.guide.firstConversation.body: Type in the input box, or click a suggested opener, then press send (or Ctrl+Enter). What just happened: the coordinator handled your request — it asked to call a tool (which you approved), read the project, and summarized the result. If confirming every step feels tedious, switch to “Allow all” anytime.
onboarding.guide.firstConversation.opene: Try asking: “What is this project about?”
onboarding.guide.firstConversation.title: Your first conversation
onboarding.guide.gateHint: Complete the action above to continue
onboarding.guide.gateHintBelow: Complete the action below to continue
onboarding.guide.hint.firstToolCall.body: You just triggered your first tool call. The coordinator uses tools to act on your behalf — switch the composer permission mode to control when they run.
onboarding.guide.openApp.body: Click any tile to open the app — it runs in a right-panel tab, so the main conversation stays reachable and you can switch back anytime.
onboarding.guide.openApp.title: Open an app
onboarding.guide.openSettings.body: Click here to open settings — model providers, prompts, skills, and keymaps are all configured in here. Let's open it now.
onboarding.guide.openSettings.title: Open settings
onboarding.guide.permissionMode.body: This button controls how autonomous the agent is. The default “Permission” mode is safest — the agent asks before every action. “Allow all” approves tool calls automatically when you trust the agent. “YOLO” goes fully hands-off, auto-approving plans, goals and tool calls. New users should keep “Permission”.
onboarding.guide.permissionMode.confirm: Keeping “Permission” is the safest choice — no change needed. Close the dropdown to continue.
onboarding.guide.permissionMode.title: Permission Mode
onboarding.guide.replay.desc: Replay the onboarding tour, including the action-gated steps. You can watch it again anytime.
onboarding.guide.replay.label: Replay guide
onboarding.guide.settings.about.body: This is where you are now! You can replay any tutorial from here, view build info, and check licenses.
onboarding.guide.settings.about.title: About & Tutorials
onboarding.guide.settings.developer.body: Developer settings include environment variables, LSP configuration, and other advanced options.
onboarding.guide.settings.entry.body: The settings panel lets you configure model providers, prompts, skills, keyboard shortcuts, and more. Click the gear icon to open it.
onboarding.guide.settings.entry.title: Settings
onboarding.guide.settings.prompt.body: Manage reusable prompt fragments and profiles. Prompts can be scoped globally or per-agent.
onboarding.guide.settings.prompt.title: Prompts
onboarding.guide.settings.provider.body: Configure your LLM API keys and model providers here. You can add multiple providers and switch between them.
onboarding.guide.settings.provider.title: Model Providers
onboarding.guide.settings.skill.body: Skills are reusable capability modules that extend what agents can do. Create custom skills or import from the store.
onboarding.guide.settings.skill.title: Skills
onboarding.guide.sidebar.body: The sidebar is your navigation hub. Use “New Chat” to start a fresh conversation with the coordinator, or “New Agent” to create a dedicated agent for a specific project. You can also switch between projects and agents here.
onboarding.guide.sidebar.title: Sidebar — your navigation
onboarding.guide.sidebarToggle.body: This button shows or hides the left sidebar. The sidebar holds your projects, agents, and the New Chat entry — on narrow screens it starts collapsed, and you can reopen it here at any time.
onboarding.guide.sidebarToggle.title: Sidebar toggle
onboarding.guide.targetMissing: This element is not visible right now. If it is inside a collapsed sidebar, closed panel, or unopened menu, open that first — the tour picks it up automatically.
onboarding.guide.tools.at.body: Typing @ opens the mention list: workspace agents first — selecting one pins an agent-chat tag into the context — plus project file paths. Use it for multi-agent collaboration or to scope the discussion to files.
onboarding.guide.tools.at.title: @ — mention agents and files
onboarding.guide.tools.bang.body: Start a message with ! and send: instead of going to the agent it opens a confirmation that creates a backlog card and opens it. Capture a thought or todo without breaking the conversation.
onboarding.guide.tools.bang.title: ! — quick note to Backlog
onboarding.guide.tools.body: The composer supports five special prefixes: / commands & modes, ! quick note, @ mentions, # card references, $ file references. This tour introduces each — just hit Next, no typing required.
onboarding.guide.tools.bundles.body: Bundles are mountable capability packs: files, git, shell, SSH, browser, web search, image/video generation, interface controls, tutoring (tutor) and more. Ask the coordinator in plain language to mount one — e.g. "mount tutor and teach me workflows".
onboarding.guide.tools.bundles.title: Bundles — the agent's tool belt
onboarding.guide.tools.dollar.body: Typing $ searches project files by path. Unlike @, it matches files only for precise scoping; the selected path enters the context and the agent reads the file directly.
onboarding.guide.tools.dollar.title: $ — reference files by path
onboarding.guide.tools.hash.body: Typing # searches project wiki cards (concepts, tasks, docs); selecting one inserts the card reference into the conversation so the agent works from existing project knowledge.
onboarding.guide.tools.hash.title: # — reference project cards
onboarding.guide.tools.modes.body: Modes are working styles mounted on an agent; type the slash name to mount: /workflow task-graph orchestration; /goal focused goal execution; /worktree isolated git worktree coding; /memory memory management; /scheduler scheduled tasks. A badge appears next to the composer and can be removed anytime.
onboarding.guide.tools.modes.title: Modes — /workflow /goal /worktree /memory /scheduler
onboarding.guide.tools.slash.body: Typing / opens the menu: builtin commands (/clear history, /compact context, /recompact from scratch, /dream memory consolidation, /help), mounted skills, and mode entries. Keep typing to filter; arrow keys select, Enter completes.
onboarding.guide.tools.slash.title: / — commands, skills and mode entries
onboarding.guide.tools.summary.body: These slash commands and shortcuts are your toolbox. Type / anytime to see the full list, or trigger them quickly from the omnibox (top search bar).
onboarding.guide.tools.summary.title: Your toolbox
onboarding.guide.tools.title: Common tools
onboarding.guide.viewModes.body: This cluster switches what the main area shows: chat, multi-console, browser, and more. Modes share the same session, so switching never loses context. Click the arrow to see the full list.
onboarding.guide.viewModes.title: Switch view modes
onboarding.guide.workflow.body: Type /workflow plus your goal and the coordinator automatically breaks the task into a dependency graph of task cards, dispatches them to workers, has reviewers check them, and aggregates the results. Complex tasks need no manual step-by-step management.
onboarding.guide.workflow.canvas.body: Each block on the canvas is a task (a single step); arrows show dependencies — B won’t start until A is done. The coordinator advances them in order automatically.
onboarding.guide.workflow.canvas.title: The workflow canvas
onboarding.guide.workflow.summary.body: This is sporemind’s core loop: intent → break down → auto-execute → review → aggregate. You give the direction; the agents get it done.
onboarding.guide.workflow.summary.title: The core loop
onboarding.guide.workflow.title: /workflow — the core capability
onboarding.guide.workflow.view.body: After typing /workflow plus your goal in the composer, send it — the coordinator starts decomposing the task. Then open the view list here and pick Workflow to see the task dependency graph and its progress on the canvas.
onboarding.guide.workflow.view.title: Switch to the workflow view

toolGuide.title: Tool Guide
toolGuide.tools.atMention.description: Type @ followed by a keyword to list loaded agents (the current agent excluded); picking one links that agent into the conversation as a chat mount for cross-agent collaboration.
toolGuide.tools.atMention.title: @ Link Agents
toolGuide.tools.cardMention.description: Type # followed by a keyword to search the current project's cards. Picking one attaches it to your message as a link badge, sent to the agent as a card reference — use it for knowledge, task, or design cards.
toolGuide.tools.cardMention.title: # Reference Cards
toolGuide.tools.fileMention.description: Type $ followed by a keyword to search project files in a dropdown; picking one attaches the file as a reference that goes out with the message.
toolGuide.tools.fileMention.title: $ Reference Files
toolGuide.tools.goal.description: Type /goal followed by your objective and the agent enters focused execution mode, working continuously until the goal is reached. Great for well-defined tasks like “refactor this module” or “fix all compile errors”.
toolGuide.tools.goal.title: /goal — Focused Execution Mode
toolGuide.tools.mounts.description: The / menu lists more than commands: its Bundle and Mode entries mount components onto the current agent when selected. Bundles add tool capabilities (e.g. web search, file tools); modes change how the agent works (e.g. the workflow mode). Mounted components appear as badges above the input — click × to unmount.
toolGuide.tools.mounts.title: Mounting Bundles & Modes
toolGuide.tools.omnibox.description: A global palette opened with Ctrl/⌘+K or the sidebar search button. Opened empty it shows a set of quick actions: new agent, new project, switch view (conversation / topology / files / problems / approvals / notes / SSH / multiconsole), open settings, import or export chat history; type to filter and run any action.
toolGuide.tools.omnibox.title: Omnibox Quick Actions
toolGuide.tools.quickNote.description: Start a message with ! followed by any text; when sent, it is not delivered to the agent but shows a confirmation to create a backlog card. Perfect for jotting down ideas or to-dos without interrupting the conversation.
toolGuide.tools.quickNote.title: ! Quick Note to Backlog
toolGuide.tools.slashCommands.descriptio: Type / in the composer anytime to see the full slash command list — a fast way to trigger common features such as /goal, /workflow, and /clear.
toolGuide.tools.slashCommands.title: Slash Commands (/)
toolGuide.tools.workflow.description: Type /workflow with your objective and the coordinator automatically decomposes it into a dependency graph of task cards, dispatches them to workers, has reviewers audit the results, and aggregates the outcome. No manual step management needed for complex work.
toolGuide.tools.workflow.title: /workflow — Workflow Capability
